bun test > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'test exit=%s\n' "$?"; bun run typecheck > /dev/null 2>&1; printf 'typecheck exit=%s\n' "$?"
perl -pi -e 's/\(http\.actingAs\((author|other)\) as TestApp\)/http.actingAs($1)/g' tests/PostUpdate.test.ts && grep -n "actingAs" tests/PostUpdate.test.ts

result:
Both `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (6 tests, 3 files) pass.

`PostController.update()` was reading `await this.request.json()` and passing the raw body to `Post.forceUpdate()`, which bypasses both the `PostPayloadSchema` validation and the `Post.fillable` allowlist — so any key the client sent, `authorId` included, was written straight to the row. I changed it (`app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:88-97`) to validate with `this.validateBody(PostPayloadSchema)` — the same schema `store()` and the `posts.update` route declaration already use — and to write via `Post.update()` instead of `forceUpdate()`. Zod strips keys outside `title`/`excerpt`/`body`, so `authorId` and `createdAt` never reach the write, the required/length rules apply again (invalid edits now throw a `ValidationException` → `422` before any DB write), and `Post.update()` keeps the fillable allowlist in force as a second layer. Authorization still runs before validation, so non-authors keep getting `403`. I also added `tests/PostUpdate.test.ts`, a feature test covering the four cases from the report: a smuggled `authorId` leaves ownership with the original author, an empty title returns `422` with the post unchanged, an extra `createdAt` is not written, and a non-author edit is still refused with `403`.
